parts.text: State what is meant by the internal energy of a system.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.stem:
An ideal gas undergoes a cycle of changes as shown in Fig. 2.1.

{{figure:figure_2_1.png}}

At point P, the gas has volume $950\ \text{cm}^3$, pressure $2.10 \times 10^5\ \text{Pa}$ and temperature $280\ \text{K}$.

The gas is heated at constant volume and $97.0\ \text{J}$ of thermal energy is transferred to the gas. Its pressure and temperature change so that the gas is at point Q on Fig. 2.1.

The gas then undergoes the change from point Q to point R and then from point R back to point P, as shown on Fig. 2.1.

Some energy changes that take place during the cycle PQRP are shown in Fig. 2.2.

| {{blank}} | change P $\rightarrow$ Q | change Q $\rightarrow$ R | change R $\rightarrow$ P |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| thermal energy transferred to gas / J | +97.0 | 0 | {{answer}} |
| work done on gas / J | {{answer}} | −42.5 | +37.0 |
| increase in internal energy of gas / J | {{answer}} | {{answer}} | {{answer}} |

Fig. 2.2
parts.text:
State the total change in internal energy of the gas during the complete cycle PQRP.
Explain your answer.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text:
